# R4AOP

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/SidraAdil/R4AOP/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SidraAdil/R4AOP/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

R4AOP gives R users access to the [AOP-Wiki](https://aopwiki.org) through its
REST API. Adverse Outcome Pathways, Key Events, Key Event Relationships,
stressors, chemicals and genes are retrieved by calling a function with
arguments, and are returned as tibbles that fit straight into an R workflow.
The AOP-Wiki RDF data are normally queried with SPARQL; for the routine tasks
covered here, the package removes that step.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("SidraAdil/R4AOP")
```

## Example

Find the Adverse Outcome Pathways that describe liver fibrosis, then follow one
of them to its Key Events and genes.

```{r example}
library(R4AOP)

fibrosis <- aop_list(q = "liver fibrosis")
fibrosis[, c("id", "title", "oecd_status")]
```

`aop_summary()` gives the overview of one AOP: its Key Events in causal order,
from the molecular initiating event to the adverse outcome, with the OECD
status, the taxonomic applicability and the stressors in the header.

```{r summary}
aop_summary(38)
```

```{r genes}
genes <- aop_genes(38)
nrow(genes)
table(genes$detected_by)
```

Genes are linked to individual Key Events, so each Key Event can be treated as
a candidate gene set. The molecular initiating event and the adverse outcome
are marked in the titles, in green and red, and a Key Event without gene links
is shown with an empty bar:

```{r plot, fig.height = 4}
aop_plot_genes(38)
```

Key Events are also described in ontology terms, as a biological process, an
optional biological object and an action. Blank cells mark components that
AOP-Wiki does not record:

```{r components, fig.height = 4}
aop_plot_components(38)
```

The same data can be entered from the other side. Starting from a stressor,
`stressor_aops()` returns the AOPs it is used in and the adverse outcomes they
end in:

```{r stressor}
stressor_aops("hexachlorobenzene")[, c("aop_id", "aop_title", "ao_title")]
```

The gene links can also be returned as a `GeneSetCollection`, one gene set
per Key Event, which passes straight to Bioconductor enrichment tools:

```{r gene-sets}
gsc <- ke_gene_sets(38)
names(gsc)
```

## Main functions

| Topic | Functions |
|---|---|
| AOPs | `aop_list()`, `aop_get()`, `aop_key_events()`, `aop_kers()`, `aop_stressors()`, `aop_chemicals()`, `aop_genes()`, `aop_methods()` |
| Key Events | `ke_list()`, `mie_list()`, `ao_list()`, `ke_get()`, `ke_aops()`, `ke_upstream()`, `ke_downstream()`, `ke_mies()`, `ke_adverse_outcomes()`, `ke_stressors()`, `ke_chemicals()` |
| Relationships | `ker_list()`, `ker_get()` |
| Stressors and chemicals | `stressor_list()`, `stressor_get()`, `stressor_aops()`, `chemical_list()`, `chemical_get()`, `chemical_aops()`, `chemical_key_events()`, `chemical_pathways()` |
| Genes and search | `gene_list()`, `gene_get()`, `ke_gene_sets()`, `aop_search()` |
| Key Event Components | `ke_components()`, `aop_components()`, `aop_plot_components()` |
| Summaries | `aop_summary()`, `aop_gene_summary()`, `aop_plot_genes()` |
| Dataset | `aop_dataset_info()`, `aop_data_version()`, `aop_cache_clear()` |

Responses are cached for the session, and list endpoints are paginated
automatically, so a call such as `ke_list()` returns all Key Events rather than
the first page.

## Reproducibility

AOP-Wiki is curated continuously. Every result carries the version of the data
it came from, which can be reported alongside an analysis:

```{r version}
aop_data_version(fibrosis)
```

## Data source and licence

Data come from the [AOP-Wiki RDF](https://aopwiki.rdf.bigcat-bioinformatics.org)
API, maintained by the Department of Translational Genomics (TGX) at Maastricht
University, and are licensed
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). The package
code is licensed MIT.

When using R4AOP, please cite both the package and AOP-Wiki.
